knee_flex.source: Seated leg curl guides (Fitness Volt, Sweat, NASM): start with the legs straight without locking the knees (0 degrees); curl until the knees bend to about 90 to 110 degrees or as far as the machine allows with good form (illustrative midpoint 100 degrees)

hip_flex.source: Seated leg curl mistake guides (Gravitus, Wenzel Coaching): keep the hips pinned to the seat and the pelvis neutral through the whole set, a narrow band around the seated 90-degree hip angle

muscles.peakSource: Seated leg curl guides: pause for a moment at the bottom of the curl, feeling the contraction through the hamstrings, so effort is highest through that hold

mistake.name: Hips up, momentum down

tells.text: The hips lift off the seat to help curl the weight.
The pad kicks down and flies back instead of a controlled curl.

mistake.source: Seated leg curl mistake guides (Gravitus, Wenzel Coaching): a hip thrust to move the pad shifts tension off the hamstrings and onto the lower back; kicking the weight down and letting it fly back removes the controlled tension the hamstring needs

sources: Contact fact (ankle strap / leg pad): the pad sits between the calf and ankle, adjusted to rest just above the knees on the thighs (Fitness Volt); a real-world description, not a numeric `machine.settings` value this research can cite
